result.title: Key Distinctions: How Do Private Markets Differ from Public Markets?
result.summary: The text introduces a due diligence questionnaire for evaluating private-market partners, explaining that private investments differ from daily-liquid public funds such as mutual funds and ETFs. Success depends less on standard performance, risk, and alpha metrics and more on harder-to-quantify strengths, including deal sourcing, information advantages, underwriting, valuation accuracy, and industry relationships. Liquid private-market funds also face distinct operational challenges: balancing inflows and investment deployment, setting redemption terms, managing layered fees, and using leverage. Accordingly, conventional approaches to evaluating firms, strategies, and risk management must be adapted for interval funds and tailored to each asset class. The questionnaire is intended to guide assessment of these qualitative and operational factors, but is only a starting point, not an exhaustive due diligence checklist.

result.title: GENERAL QUESTIONS
key_items: Investment Risk; Fees; Operations & Liquidity; Valuation; Governance; Red Flag Questions
result.summary: A due-diligence questionnaire covering the firm’s ownership, assets and funds by asset class, private-market experience, investment staffing, and institutional or retail clientele; strategy, market opportunity, portfolio exposures, deal sourcing and rejection, investment decisions, market conditions, and benchmarks; risk controls, including leverage, private/public exposure, position and sector limits, stress testing, and early warnings; fees, incentive terms, leverage costs, other charges, and breakpoints; subscriptions, redemptions, liquidity restrictions and gates, flow management, redemption history, illiquid-asset sales, strategy and return effects of periodic liquidity, and investor paperwork; administration, NAV controls, audits, valuation methods, frequency, fair-value levels, Level 3 procedures, and below-cost holdings; governance, track records, key-person succession, investment committees, and allocation policies; and red flags involving departures, complaints, regulatory matters, litigation, capacity, fund closure, and principal strategy risks.

result.title: Private Equity and Private Credit Due Diligence
result.summary: The page requests private equity information on deal sourcing, GP access, vintage-level returns (IRR, TVPI, DPI; gross and net), performance by investment type, deployment plans, strategy mix, and return drivers. It also covers pacing and distribution modeling, vintage and industry composition, concentration and position sizes, redemption liquidity, credit facilities, and responses to redemption stress. For private credit, it asks about underwriting, average LTV and maturity, debt seniority, sector allocation, yield, industry and geographic diversification, and private/public and fund/direct exposure. Risk questions address performance monitoring, default management, non-performing assets, historical defaults and losses, PIK exposure, and concentration. Operations questions cover daily liquidity, duration distribution, other liquidity sources, facility balances, and possible forced sales to meet redemptions.

result.title: Hedge Fund and Real Asset Due Diligence
result.summary: A due diligence questionnaire covering hedge fund and real asset investment strategies, risks, and operations. For hedge funds, it asks about investment vehicles, turnover, return targets and history, strategy allocations and limits; portfolio-wide and underlying liquidity, constraints, position sizing, leverage, stress testing, volatility behavior, and hedging; and manager background checks, operational failures, review frequency, and service providers. For real assets, it covers economic and market-cycle positioning, income versus total return, geographic and asset diversification, risk/return, performance, and benchmarks; leverage, long-term regulatory, environmental and obsolescence risks, and liquidity; and redemptions, asset sales, capital spending, property improvements, and NAV volatility. The footer provides Calamos contact details and Calamos/Aksia copyright and trademark notices.
